clue.text: Condemn one knowing little about British opera company

indicators.note: the word for a dim pupil goes round the opera company, enclosing it

parts.note: a dunce is someone who knows little
ENO is English National Opera

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses an ignorant commentator on a British opera company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one knowing little' is a paraphrase for a slow pupil, and 'about' makes it wrap round the opera company's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce someone is to condemn them publicly; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Race that may be cut to make an impression

definitions.text: that may be cut to make an impression

explanation.definitionFit: A dash is a short sprint, and 'cut a dash' means look impressive.

clue.text: Animal rescuer's unhelpful response to doctor's request

parts.note: a flat no is an unhelpful reply
a doctor examining a throat asks the patient to say ah

explanation.surface: A man who saves animals gives a refusal when a doctor asks something.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'rescuer' is 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch saved the animals by taking them aboard the ark before the flood.

clue.text: In university the corrupt state is dishonourable

indicators.note: the scrambled article is put inside the short word for university
corrupt means spoiled or distorted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A dishonest condition prevails at the college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal, not a link word; 'state' is a US state, abbreviated as in postal addresses of old.
explanation.definitionFit: Unethical conduct breaches moral principles, which makes it dishonourable.

clue.text: First-class product of 12's sporting contest

parts.note: champion as an adjective means excellent
12 across is the builders of vessels, whose product is a vessel

explanation.surface: Top-quality output from twelve in a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A championship is a competition held to decide a sports champion.

clue.text: Device interchanging parts of bookies' sign language

indicators.note: the two halves of the bookies' signalling word swap places

parts.note: tic-tac is the hand-signal code used by British racecourse bookmakers

explanation.surface: A gadget that swaps around the hand signals bookmakers use at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: TIC-TAC is the arm-waving code British bookmakers use at racecourses; 'interchanging parts of' swaps its halves to give TAC+TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a ploy or stratagem, which is one sense of device.

clue.text: It's reportedly spoken of the listener

indicators.note: signals a word that is heard to sound like another

parts.note: oral means spoken

explanation.surface: A remark about speech from a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aural means relating to the ear and hearing, hence to someone listening.

clue.text: Sensitivity is inclined to restrict birds of prey

indicators.note: the verb phrase hems the birds in by surrounding them

parts.note: tends means is inclined
ernes are sea eagles

explanation.surface: A tender heart is reluctant to cage hawks and eagles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'birds of prey' are sea eagles, a crossword staple; 'is inclined' must keep its S, which ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderness is sensitivity, whether of feeling or of a sore spot.

clue.text: Angry about bed being put outside for lurcher

parts.note: cross means angry

indicators.note: the bed's letters are placed round the short word for about

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A furious owner's bed is thrown out of the house because of the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: A lurcher is a dog bred from a greyhound and another breed such as a collie.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a hybrid dog, an example of a crossbreed.

clue.text: It's used to separate characters in the pool

definitions.text: It's used to separate characters in the pool

parts.words: It's used to separate characters in the pool
parts.note: read as a keyboard part pressed by typists in a typing pool to put gaps between letters, not a divider in a swimming pool

explanation.surface: Something keeps the people apart at the swimming baths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' are typed letters and 'the pool' is an office typing pool, not swimmers in a pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The long key on a keyboard inserts gaps between typed letters, keeping words apart.

clue.text: Sergeant, possibly, on little sibling's horse

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: bro is a short form of brother
a sergeant is one kind of NCO, non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A soldier rides his younger brother's horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronco is a wild or half-tamed horse of the American West.

clue.text: Like tubers near a northern resort?

definitions.text: Like tubers near a northern resort?

indicators.note: taken as a verb, sort again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Potatoes near a northern seaside town?
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town but is a verb, re-sort; the whole clue also describes the answer, tubers being found below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubers grow beneath the soil, which is what subterranean means: under the earth.

clue.text: They may make a packet on stocks

definitions.text: They may make a packet on stocks

parts.words: They may make a packet on stocks
parts.note: read not as stock-market traders getting rich but as builders of a packet boat on the stocks, the timber frame a vessel stands on while built

explanation.surface: Traders make a fortune on the stock market.
explanation.walkthrough: A packet is a mail boat and the stocks are the frame supporting a ship under construction.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who build vessels construct them on the stocks, packet boats included.

clue.text: Friends accept religious instruction to a significant extent

indicators.note: the two friendly words take in the abbreviation between them

parts.note: a mate is a friend
an ally is a friend
RI is religious instruction, a British school subject

explanation.surface: Pals welcome Sunday school lessons a good deal.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'Friends', supplies two different synonyms which sit either side of the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Materially means substantially or considerably, to a significant degree.

clue.text: Considerate like one of Rodin's subjects?

definitions.meaning: Rodin's famous statue The Thinker is lost in contemplation

explanation.definitionFit: The word means kind to others and also deep in thought, like Rodin's Thinker.

clue.text: Senior officer's assistant seizing house for specific purpose

indicators.note: the assistant's letters grab and hold the house abbreviation inside

parts.note: ADC is aide-de-camp, an officer's assistant

explanation.surface: A general's aide commandeers a building for a particular mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc is Latin for 'to this', describing something arranged for one particular purpose.

clue.text: One goes faster than the leading dog

definitions.meaning: someone who outpaces another in a race
the lead animal running out in front of a team of sled dogs

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both one who outpaces others and the lead dog in a harnessed team.

clue.text: Causing displeasure? It's not willingly admitted

definitions.meaning: a visitor or thing nobody is glad to let in

explanation.definitionFit: The word means disagreeable and also not received gladly into a place.

clue.text: Peer is extremely eager for reply that might make one point

definitions.text: reply that might make one point

parts.note: a peer is an equal

indicators.note: the very ends of the word eager are taken

explanation.surface: A lord is very keen to answer back.
explanation.walkthrough: A football equaliser is the reply goal that turns a defeat into a draw, worth one league point.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal that levels the score answers the opponents' goal and earns a draw, one point.

clue.text: Rubbish found in desert

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both refuse and a barren tract of wild land.

clue.text: Unfriendly bishop in modern infirmary given drug

parts.note: in means fashionable or modern

indicators.note: the bishop's letter is placed within the word for infirmary

parts.note: an infirmary is a hospital
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A cold churchman lies in a new hospital being treated with medication.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhospitable place or person is unwelcoming, which is to say unfriendly.

clue.text: Mechanical system thus used to digest English Bible

indicators.note: the word for thus swallows the letters inside it

parts.note: so means thus
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A machine for absorbing English scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A servo is a servomechanism, an automatic device that controls a larger machine.

clue.text: As which Snug the joiner was a roaring success

definitions.text: As which Snug the joiner was a roaring success

parts.words: As which Snug the joiner was a roaring success
parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream the joiner Snug plays a beast whose part is just roaring in the mechanicals' play

explanation.surface: A carpenter has a triumph in an amateur play.
explanation.walkthrough: Snug is the joiner among Shakespeare's mechanicals; 'roaring success' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug's role in Pyramus and Thisbe is the big cat, whose part is mostly roaring.

clue.text: Sound fellow in flexible armour

indicators.note: signals a word heard as another of the same pronunciation

parts.note: a fellow is a male

explanation.surface: A healthy man in chain armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'healthy' describing the fellow, but signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail is armour of linked metal rings, flexible unlike plate.

clue.text: They'll theoretically die at the end of time

definitions.text: They'll theoretically die at the end of time

parts.words: They'll theoretically die at the end of time
parts.note: read as prisoners serving a whole-life term who in theory leave only when they die at the end of their time inside

explanation.surface: A reflection on the fate of everything when the universe ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' is a prison sentence, not cosmic time.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners sentenced to life imprisonment are said to serve life, ending only with death.

clue.text: Woman in charge in Valentine and Proteus's city

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed inside the name of the Italian city

parts.note: Valentine and Proteus are Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen of Verona
IC is the usual short form for a person or officer who is the one responsible

explanation.surface: A woman takes command in the Shakespearean city of two gentlemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Cry out in pain like a coward

parts.note: to yell is to cry out
ow is an exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: Someone screams with pain, acting cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is an informal word for cowardly.

clue.text: Conclude one's out of tack? Like hell!

parts.note: to infer is to conclude

indicators.note: the numeral letter is removed from the word for a tack

parts.note: a tack is a small nail
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sailor works out he is off course and exclaims with disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tack' looks nautical but is a small nail; NAIL minus I gives NAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal means belonging to hell, so it describes something like hell.
